title: Apple Unveils Its First Touchscreen Laptop
paragraphs: For many years, Apple refused to make laptops with touchscreens. Now, the company has finally changed its mind.

On October 28, 2026, at an event in Los Angeles, Apple unveiled its first touchscreen laptops: the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display. The laptops come in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes and are powered by Apple's M5 Pro or M5 Max chips.

The new models have an OLED display that can reach a brightness of up to 2,000 nits. Users can touch the screen to scroll, zoom in and out, drag and drop items and interact directly with creative software. The laptops can be configured with up to 128 gigabytes of memory and 16 terabytes of storage, and Apple says their batteries can last up to 24 hours. The 14-inch model weighs about 3 pounds. The laptops also run Apple's latest operating system, macOS 27, which brings a feature called Dynamic Island to the Mac for the first time.

However, the new laptops are expensive. The 14-inch model with an M5 Pro chip starts at $2,899, while the 16-inch model with an M5 Max chip costs $4,799. Customers could start ordering them on October 28, and they became available on November 6.

The decision marks a major change for Apple. In 2010, Steve Jobs, Apple's co-founder, described touchscreens on laptops as "ergonomically terrible." In 2012, Tim Cook, who was then Apple's CEO, compared combining a laptop with a tablet to combining a toaster with a refrigerator. Meanwhile, laptops running Windows have had touchscreens for more than a decade.

According to Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer, the new MacBook Pro is a monumental step forward for the Mac. Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said that Apple had always been wrong to resist touchscreens.

However, some people pointed out that the new models use the same M5 chips as some existing Macs, so the touchscreen and display may be their main attraction, rather than a big improvement in performance.
